addTheFirstStreamChecksStart: Add the first stream — checks start right away.
connectionSetupHint: Connections are kept between checks, so every five minutes each stream is checked on a connection made on purpose: this is how long the name lookup, the connection and TLS take. Over all streams.
entryRedirectsHint: How many redirects a request to the stream's address follows on average before it gets a playlist. Growth means the servers pass requests on to each other.
entryTimeHint: How long a request to the stream's address takes with all the redirects it follows: the work of the balancer, not of the stream. Over all streams.
howManyStreamsWereInEach: How many streams were in each status; a stream counts by its worst status within the step
howManyTimesAPlaylistCame: How many times a playlist came from a different server than the last time, over all streams
lossByServerHint: How many TCP segments the monitor had to send to a server again, per request; a request usually fits in one segment, so this is nearly the share of requests that needed a retransmission. It is loss in one direction — from the monitor to the server; loss on the way back, in the data of the segment itself, shows as packets out of order. Fractions of a percent are usual on the internet. It is usually single long-lived connections that lose, not a server as a whole, so the difference between servers is largely random: it shows which server such connections happen to go to now.
lossyServer: More than 5 % of the requests to the server needed a retransmission
playlistRequestTimeOverAllStreams: Playlist request time over all streams: average and 95th percentile
requestsByServerHint: How many requests of the checks per second every server answers: it shows how the balancer spreads the streams and whether a server has dropped out.
roundTripTimeHint: By the kernel's count on the connections the checks use, over all streams. The kernel times a segment until it is acknowledged, and a server often acknowledges a request together with its answer, so the figure is a few milliseconds above the delay of the network alone. What is worth watching is how it changes.
rttByServerHint: Round trip time to every server by the kernel's count, from all vantage points together. A few milliseconds above the delay of the network alone; what is worth watching is the difference between servers and how it changes.
selfCPUHint: How many processor cores the monitor's server itself takes, and how many its whole container does, with the programs it runs (the decoder of pictures is one). Agents are not counted here.
selfMemoryHint: The memory of the server's container, or of the process when the container has no limit.
signsOfLoss: Loss between the monitor and the servers
signsOfLossHint: By the kernel's count, over all streams. Retransmissions are segments the monitor had to send again: loss on the way to the servers, each one holds a request back by 0.2 s or more. Out of order are segments from the servers that did not arrive in sequence: the monitor cannot count what was lost on the way to it, and this is the only sign of such loss, though the network may also just reorder them.
streamsAndTheirStatusHistoryWill: Streams and their status history will appear here
streamsAreAddedByAnAdministrator: Streams are added by an administrator.
sumOfTheBitratesOfStreams: Streams: the sum of the bitrates of streams whose segments are checked — what viewers of all of them would download. Checks: what the monitor really downloads to check them, from all vantage points together: playlists, and as much of the segments as the level of each stream takes.
timeToTheFirstByteOf: Time to the first byte of a segment over all streams: average and 95th percentile
totalBitrateOfStreams: Bitrate of streams and traffic of checks
trafficOfChecks: Downloaded by the checks, from all vantage points
unavailablePlaylistsSegmentErrorsSegment: Unavailable playlists, segment errors, segments missed between checks, stalls of the player model
whichServersAnsweredInTheLast: Which servers answered in the last five minutes and the status of the streams they serve
